_about: What LiteMind is running: DeepSeek-V2-Lite. Every number here is derived from config.json, not measured, and matches what `LiteMind.exe models --inspect` reports. This file is documentation only - nothing reads it.

identity._note: A mixture-of-experts model: it holds 15.7 billion parameters but runs only 2.4 billion of them for any one token. That gap is the whole reason this project works on a laptop.
identity.name: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
identity.kind: base model - it continues text, it does not answer questions

layers._note: 27 decoder layers. Layer 0 is a normal dense feed-forward layer; the other 26 replace it with a mixture of experts.

experts._note: This is the number that matters. Each MoE layer holds 64 routed experts, but the router picks only 6 of them per token. 2 shared experts run for every token regardless.

one_expert._note: Three matrices - gate, up and down - forming one SwiGLU feed-forward block.

routing._note: Softmax runs over all 64 experts BEFORE the top-6 cut. norm_topk_prob is false, so the six weights are raw probabilities that deliberately do not sum to one.

attention._note: Multi-head latent attention. Keys and values are not stored per head; the hidden state is compressed to a kv_lora_rank latent and expanded by kv_b_proj. The rotary part of the key is decoupled - one vector shared by all heads.
attention.q_lora_note: 0 means q_proj is a single dense matrix

positional_encoding._note: YaRN-scaled rotary embedding. DeepSeek reshapes the rotary channels from [d] to [d/2, 2] and transposes before rotating; rotating the raw interleaved layout pairs the wrong channels and produces fluent-looking noise.

vocabulary._note: Byte-level BPE. The tokenizer holds two more entries than config.json declares, which are added special tokens.

parameters._note: Only 15.6% of the model runs per token. Everything except the routed experts is active every step.

memory._note: The always-hot part is touched every step and the OS keeps it resident. The routed experts are what streaming exists for.

kv_cache._note: float32, stored expanded rather than as the latent. key_rope is one vector shared by all heads, which is why it is not multiplied by the head count.

per_token_cost._note: What one generated token costs. Multiply by (prompt tokens + generated tokens) for a whole run - prefill is sequential, so a prompt token costs the same as a generated one.
per_token_cost.minimum_useful_expert_cache_note: A single token touches this much of the expert weights. An --expert-cache budget below it evicts every expert before it can be reused, giving a 0% hit rate by construction.
